title: The field job
why: Open 0, New 1, Miss 1, Reach 2. The rules, their starting numbers and their names are settled in the brief, and the spec step's probe (probe.diff) ran them on the retro maps. Done is exact: the tests it writes, fields off equal to the base on every map, and fields on near the probe's y8. It is adapted from split, change and recentre. It reaches every turn: reap, the move step, the harvest and tend. The piece's Shape line called this the clay. Scored at 4, it isn't the hard part, so the piece is Easel and Canvas (spec.md, Shape). About 11 files, 550 lines: fields.rs (~180 new), clans.rs (~40), data.rs (FIELD and Config, ~45), actors.rs (recentre's target, ~10), land.rs, map.rs, events.rs, world.rs, core/tests/fields.rs (~250), cli/tests/save.rs pins, engine/CLAUDE.md.

title: The judge, the control, the feed and the design edits
why: Open 0, New 1, Miss 1, Reach 1. Every count, the sixth run and the text are named in the brief, after judge_ring.rs's pattern. A test it writes catches the counts, and spec-review.md's 'y8, tame 1' rows catch a count far off. It reaches the judge and the sweep, not the turn. About 13 files, 500 lines: judge_fields.rs (~200 new), judge.rs (~15), sweep_judge.rs (~20), sweep_fields.rs (~150 new, keeping sweep_judge.rs under 600), sweep_text.rs (~40), game_judge.rs, feed.js, check.mjs, sounds.json, core/tests/fields.rs (~60), clans.md and actors.md (three lines), engine/CLAUDE.md, judge.md.

title: The page
why: Open 2, New 1, Miss 1, Reach 0. The rows, the keys, the layer and the script are settled. How the furrows read at a glance among the floodplain wash is judged by eye from fields.png (Open 2). The layer follows floodplains.js and the panels follow their neighbours. fields.mjs, which it writes, catches a missing row or layer. About 12 files, 300 lines new, and up to 250 moved if panels.js splits into panels-land.js: web/src/lib.rs (~30), panels.js (~50), map/layers/fields.js (~45), map/view.js, bar.js, atlas.json, cli/src/view.rs, www/play/fields.mjs (~90), all.mjs, check-stage.mjs (~30), the two screenshots.

title: Fields that pay
why: Open 4, New 1, Miss 3, Reach 2. Seven numbers are tuned together against nine bounds on the retro maps. The spec-review's runs (spec-review.md) show the starving bound is a rule's work, not a number's: with bound 2 holding grain at 0.75 or more, margin, home rule and floodplain ground leave starving at 1.30-1.34 times the control, and only a lower yield moved it. Only the sweep catches a miss, and the rules run every turn. Opus low on the canvas rung. I expect it to run eight to twelve settings, two at a time at about 6 minutes a pair, find who the starving gatherers are, and change the field rule that squeezes them. About 4 files, 150 lines: data.rs, fields.rs, perhaps clans.rs, core/tests/fields.rs for any rule it changes, canvas.md.

twin.why: A rung below: does a canvas whose last bound needs a rule change, with the judge printing every bound as pass or miss, need Opus? I expect Sonnet high to run a grid of numbers, meet bounds 1-5 and 7, and stop with bound 6 passing only past the floor or an ask with the nearest setting. I expect Opus more likely to find why gatherers starve beside farmers and change the rule that causes it, passing bound 6 with room. Both write canvas.md from the same seven maps, the same no-fields control and the same --floor sweep, so the pick reads them side by side.

title: Review the piece
why: The goal is Standing against a control on the retro maps, and fields are an economy every later M4 piece stands on and a mechanic the player meets every turn: Opus medium.
